text.p: Typhoon Tina is currently centered about 55 miles west southwest of Okinawa, moving north at 10 mph. Tina will pass west of Okinawa during the next 6 hours, bringing rain squalls, gusty winds, and rough surf to the island. Major damage is not expected, however. Tina has top winds near 100 mph but is weakening. It is expected to be a minimal typhoon as it passes just west of Cheju near southern Korea in 48 to 60 hours. Tina remains a threat to shipping in the East China Sea.
Heavy rain and thunderstorms in Bangladesh the next few days may lead to further flooding resulting in crop and property damage.

In the USA Southwest and Rockies, thunderstorms have caused local flash flooding in portions of the region. During the next couple days, the heaviest storms will be in eastern Colorado into the plains of western Kansas, where flash flooding may occur.

Hurricane Guillermo has top winds of 130 mph but is over open waters in the eastern Pacific 1200 miles west southwest of the southern tip of Baja, moving to the west northwest. This system is a major threat to shipping. Guillermo is no threat to Hawaii at this time. It is expected to continue this track, weakening.
